title: Waiting at the Bus Stop
statement: Buses arrive at a stop as a Poisson process with an average gap of $10$ minutes. You arrive at a random time. What is the expected length, in minutes, of the gap between the bus before you and the bus after you?
insight: You are more likely to land in a long gap. With memorylessness, the time back to the last bus and forward to the next are each 10 on average.
redHerring: Answering 10 because the average gap is 10.
hints: Is the gap you land in a typical gap?
How long do you expect to wait for the next bus? Does the past matter?
Run time backwards: how long ago was the previous bus?
solution:
By memorylessness, the wait until the next bus is exponential with mean 10. Reversing time, a Poisson process looks the same, so the time since the previous bus is also exponential with mean 10.

The gap you sit in has expected length $10 + 10 = 20$. Long gaps cover more of the timeline, so a random time is more likely to land in one (size-biased sampling).
